clue.text: Baconian prize for film now translated into Dutch

explanation.walkthrough: 'translated into' rearranges the letters of FILM NOW and DUTCH. The Dunmow Flitch is a side of bacon awarded in an old custom at Great Dunmow in Essex to a married couple who have not quarrelled for a year and a day.
explanation.definitionFit: A flitch is a side of cured pork, the trophy of the Essex contest, so it is literally a prize made of bacon.

clue.text: Make out record, one from Old Ireland

clue.text: Three in a thousand in line to win

explanation.definitionFit: Zeros are the round symbols in the written figure, and also the marks one player draws in the grid game against crosses.

explanation.walkthrough: 'big guns' looks like slang for important lawyers; here it is artillery, ORDNANCE, with I placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative decree or local regulation, a kind of law.

clue.text: Music-makers of an old Scottish kingdom

explanation.surface: Pipers or players hail from an ancient realm in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a set of small flutes and, read as a possessive, belonging to the Scottish region north of Edinburgh.

clue.text: " That was I turned into a hart " (T Night)

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the verb inside the Galilee wedding town. Candida is the title heroine of George Bernard Shaw's play.

clue.text: Sycophancy unprofitable for one poor dog

parts.note: fawning affection shown in hope of food; in the nursery rhyme Old Mother Hubbard found the larder bare, so her poor dog gained nothing by such affection

explanation.surface: Flattery gets a poor dog nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means affection put on for what can be got, as a pet fawns on whoever feeds it.

clue.text: In a French and German context, so fallacious

explanation.walkthrough: 'In' and 'context' place the little word between the French article and the German conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsound argument is faulty or invalid, a synonym of fallacious.

clue.text: The race is to the swift catcher of fish

parts.note: swift means fast
fishermen catch fish in a net

explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes 'the race is not to the swift' from Ecclesiastes. The Fastnet Race is a famous offshore yacht race round the Fastnet Rock off southern Ireland.

clue.text: Roman malefactors dashed from new-made open-air track

clue.text: In some melodious plot Of — green " (Keats)

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means made of or belonging to the tree with grey bark and nuts called mast, describing the grove in the ode.

clue.text: More disreputable rioting is heard

explanation.definitionFit: Shadier means more dubious or of worse repute, as a shady dealer is untrustworthy.

clue.text: Elevate first citizen — sound idea from Peacock Abbey

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Love Peacock wrote the satirical novel Nightmare Abbey; the word missing from its title is what the spoken pair sounds like.
explanation.definitionFit: The first word of Peacock's novel title names a frightening dream, the idea of the book.

clue.text: Hamlet thought his father such a dog!

clue.text: To ornament steel' needs heaver's work, and a bit of play

clue.text: It comes from the heart of Nigeria or Tanzania

clue.text: Grammatically it could be the thing

clue.text: Trusting in later reform
